purpose: Encorafenib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including melanoma (a serious type of skin cancer) that has a specific gene change called a BRAF mutation. It is also used for a type of colorectal cancer (bowel cancer) that has the same BRAF mutation. It is usually given together with another medication called binimetinib or cetuximab.
how_it_works: Inside some cancer cells, there is a faulty protein made by a mutated BRAF gene that tells the cancer to grow out of control. Encorafenib works like a targeted 'off switch' — it blocks that faulty protein so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow and spread. Because it targets a specific change in cancer cells, it works differently from traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or weak, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, joint or muscle pain, skin thickening on palms or soles of feet (hand-foot syndrome), rash, hair loss, headache, and changes in blood test results such as liver enzymes or blood sugar levels.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious problems including new skin cancers, eye problems (such as vision changes or bleeding in the eye), heart rhythm changes, liver problems, bleeding, and high blood sugar. Tell your doctor right away if you notice changes in your vision, unusual bleeding, chest pounding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or signs of a new skin growth. Avoid pregnancy while taking this medication as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interact with encorafenib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 450 mg taken by mouth once a day when used with binimetinib for melanoma, or 300 mg once a day when used with cetuximab for colorectal cancer. It can be taken with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or open them. If you miss a dose and your next dose is more than 12 hours away, take it as soon as you remember; otherwise skip the missed dose.
